name: Storybook
summary: Staged scenes of layered cut shapes with parallax, where act changes are told by palette and light rather than captions. For people, stakes and an emotional arc.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: Remember the people and what was at stake, and feel the turn.
visual_job.hero: Characters or one emblematic object in a staged scene whose mood changes across acts.

use_when: There are specific people, a place and a turning point.
The feeling is the point as much as the facts.
The piece is built as acts: normal, disruption, aftermath.
avoid_when: The facts must be checked at a glance (use news-brief or data-ledger).
The subject has no people or place to stage.

alternates.when: The brief asks for night, depth or dread.

scene_grammar.formula: One specific person or place at one specific moment.
The normal, with warmth: full palette, layered depth.
Colour or light shifts; one element goes wrong.
Stakes grow: camera closer, palette narrows.
The quiet beat. Stillness is allowed only with drift and a sound under it.

motion.signature: Layered cut shapes with parallax; the act changes through palette and light.
motion.continuous_layer: Parallax drift between layers and ambient float on small elements.
avoid: A music swell laid over a fact.
Playful bounce on a tragic subject.

rules.ending: Return to the opening composition, altered; hold the last image with drift under a low sound.

short_form.closing: Reel-length films: the return to the opening composition doubles as the loop; echo one word or image from the hook in the last line.

anti_patterns.pattern: The same empty stage in most scenes.
anti_patterns.why: repeat-layout-dom fired in all three films (3-5 of 6 scenes). A recurring grid is fine when its state changes; vary the hero's position or scale between scenes.

anti_patterns.pattern: Narration over a frame that does not change for more than max_beat_gap_sec.
anti_patterns.why: Breaks the anti-laziness rule. motion-qa flagged 41 s of 70 (cloud), 44 s of 92 (fridge), 79 s of 98 (Korea) as static or low-energy. Plan one visual event per 2-3 s from measured onsets and give every scene a drift layer (Studio.space.drift).

anti_patterns.pattern: Narration that restates what the picture already says.
anti_patterns.why: In a story the picture carries the feeling; the voice should add what cannot be drawn.
anti_patterns.source: Authored from the design profile and VISION.md; not yet render-tested.

anti_patterns.pattern: A greeting, a title card or a framing sentence before the claim.
anti_patterns.why: The film starts at the sentence you would normally reach at second six. No welcome, no 'in this video', no logo sting. A stamped event opens on the date and the fact.
anti_patterns.source: ig-reel rules (Jake Schincariol, MIT), adopted 2026-11-05 via docs/short-form-lessons.md.

anti_patterns.pattern: More than one ask at the end.
anti_patterns.why: End on one action or none. Two asks split the last three seconds and the viewer does neither. A news brief usually needs none.
anti_patterns.source: ig-reel rules (Jake Schincariol, MIT), adopted 2026-11-05 via docs/short-form-lessons.md; checked by `studio.py script` (many-asks).

open_questions: Rules for depicting real casualties (restraint, figures versus faces) are not written down.

revisions.change: Initial version. Acts-by-palette approach taken from the editorial-paper-collage profile.
Added rules.short_form (cards of 6 words or fewer, the return-to-opening ending as the loop) and two anti-patterns: framing sentence before the claim, more than one ask.
